answer: Delayed Whisper Kernel Admission.** Each identity must send its first N messages with inter-arrival times fitting a kernel-estimated human baseline, enforced by a per-identity timer that rejects bursts. The rule: no reply may land faster than the fitted fable of prior gaps, so scripted mass registration stalls. An attacker pays wall-clock latency per identity—weeks to season IDs before they act—plus compute to shape traffic convincingly; parallel sybils don't compress that wait.
